This report extends the IDEA Bio fermentation report (Parts 1–2) with the omics
+ machine-learning analysis that the standard template stubs out. It predicts a
chosen metabolite **yield** from phase-3 **proteomics** using the `ml_multiomics`
library, and compares methods under leakage-free (per-bioreactor) cross-validation.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
#| tags: [parameters]

# The target compound. Defaults to psilocybin; swap to any compound in the
# yields file (see "Try another target" at the end). Examples:
#   psilocybin_ext, tryptamine_ext, psilocin_ext, Baeocystine_ext, serotonin_ext
compound = "psilocybin_ext"
```

# Part 3.1 — Overview

```{python}
#| echo: false
Markdown(
    f"- **Target:** `{res['compound']}` yield (over biomass), phase {res['phase']}\n"
    f"- **Samples:** {res['n_bioreactors']} bioreactors (one independent unit each)\n"
    f"- **Features:** {res['n_proteins']} proteins (phase-3 average per bioreactor)\n"
    f"- **Yield:** mean {res['yield_mean']:.3g}, sd {res['yield_std']:.3g}\n"
    f"- **Conditions:** " + ", ".join(f"{k} (n={v})" for k, v in res['conditions'].items())
)
```

This is a classic **low-n, high-p** problem: a few dozen samples versus thousands
of proteins. The pipeline therefore favours regularization and
*reduce-then-predict*, and validates by leaving out **whole bioreactors** so no
run leaks across the train/test split.

# Part 3.2 — Descriptive model panel (CV as a guardrail)

Each approach predicts the yield under leave-one-bioreactor-out CV. `Lasso` /
`ElasticNet` / `RandomForest` use all proteins (z-scored); `PCA→RF` and `NMF→RF`
first **reduce** the ~4,000 proteins to a few factors, then predict.

**This is not a leaderboard.** At ~28 bioreactors a single CV R² is noisy — read
the panel as *"does anything clear the predict-the-mean baseline (R²=0) without
obviously overfitting, and do the reduced models hold up?"*, not as a precise
ranking. The value of reducing the big proteomics block is interpretability and
block-balancing, described below — not winning a contest.

```{python}
#| echo: false
res["comparison"].round(3)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
comp = res["comparison"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 3.4))
ax.barh(comp["method"], comp["r2"], color="#2B6CB0")
ax.set_xlabel("Leave-one-bioreactor-out $R^2$  (0 = predict-the-mean baseline)")
ax.set_title(f"{res['compound']} yield — descriptive panel (not a ranking)")
ax.axvline(0, color="0.4", lw=0.8)
ax.invert_yaxis()
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
Markdown(
    f"Predict-the-mean baseline RMSE = {res['baseline_mean_rmse']:.3g} (R²=0). "
    "Models above the 0 line carry signal beyond the mean; treat differences "
    "between them as within-noise at this sample size, and prefer the reduced, "
    "interpretable representations for downstream hypotheses."
)
```

# Part 3.4 — How much to trust this

```{python}
#| echo: false
r = res["resolution"]
Markdown(
    f"- **Sample size:** {res['n_bioreactors']} independent bioreactors. Treat results "
    f"as **exploratory** and cross-check methods.\n"
    f"- **Statistical resolution:** with this design the finest achievable "
    f"permutation p-value is ~{r['finest_two_sided_p']:.2g} — a single p-value "
    f"cannot go below that floor, so we report effect size (R²) first.\n"
    f"- **Goal is interpretation, not a deployable predictor.** At this n we use\n"
    f"  the panel to find signal and stable, interpretable factors/proteins — not\n"
    f"  to claim a production model.\n"
    f"- **Reducing proteomics is principled preprocessing:** ~4,000 proteins → a\n"
    f"  few factors balances the (single) block and yields interpretable axes; the\n"
    f"  reducers (PCA/NMF) are standard sklearn, no parameter guesswork.\n"
    f"- **No leakage:** every fold left out whole bioreactors; no double-scaling "
    f"(data scaled once in preprocessing); NMF ran on non-negative log2 data."
)
```
